title.narrative: BF SAT Zambia

description.narrative: Millions of young people do not have access to appropriate, gender-responsive, quality SRHR education, information and services. This makes them vulnerable to unintended pregnancies, often followed by child marriage (CM). The Break Free! programme empowers adolescents and young people to make their own free and informed choices to speak out and have control over their SRH and lives. BF! is tackling root causes of gender inequality, unequal power relations and discriminatory social norms, systems, structures, policies and practices, supported by civil society and improved legislation. The project will be implemented between 2021 and 2025 by the Break Free! Consortium consisting of Plan International Netherlands, SAT and FAWE, technical partners KIT and RMT in collaboration with Dutch Embassies. It will be carried out in Burkina Faso, Ethiopia, Kenya, Malawi, Mali, Mozambique, Niger, Sudan and Zambia, in addition to a regional Pan-African component to sustain the country programmes.

The primary target group of the Break Free programme consists if girls and young women (GYW) aged 10 -24. To effectuate change in the lives of those GYW, the programme engages other stakeholders such as government, CSOs, parents and/or caretakers and the community at large in the 9 focus countries of Break Free!

The strategic programme objective of: adolescents exercise their right to live free from TP and CM, supported by civil society is contributing the above-defined impact. To achieve this strategic objective, CSOs, youth-led groups and networks will be strengthened to lobby and advocate for improved legislation and implementation to increase girls’ agency and to promote social norm change in favour of the prevention of CM/TP, and in some countries FGM/C. Although norm change takes time and the strategic objective is formulated under the ‘sphere of influence’ over which we do not have full control, the programme will report reduced prevalence of CM and TP for groups of girls in the programme locations, by 2025. The following three pathways of change lead towards the strategic programme objective.Outcome 1: Adolescent girls at risk of CM/TP access quality and safe education,Outcome 2: Duty bearers and decision-makers develop, resource and implement laws and policies that respond to adolescents’ needs, andOutcome 3: Adolescents access quality SRHR information, education and services.

title.narrative: Number of adolescents aged 10-24 reached with SRHR information/education
# of young people (female) reached with comprehensive, correct information on sexuality, HIV/AIDS, STIs, pregnancy and contraception

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of female youths (aged 10 - 24 years) that are reached by CSE though the activities implemented by the program. The indicator counts in school and out of school youths.

comment.narrative: CSE activities will apply to both in school and out of school adolescents and young people. The programme will reach in-school youths through guidance and counselling teachers and school-based clubs. Out-of-school youths will be reached through out-of-school youth champions, religious structures, and community events. Sports coaches, youth hub stars, champions of change and health facilities also be used to deliver CSE beyond the school setup. Digital technologies through Youthwyze will be intensified to align programming that suits the contemporary SRHR demands of the changing times. Through provision of mobile gadgets, young people will be used to provide information, referral making hence improving the turnaround time.

The overachievement was as a result of various strategies that the BF! utilized. These included the use of the schools based clubs, sports events where health education was done including linkages for services. The programme also conducted 20 outreaches during the period under review while through YouthWyze 14,964 young people were reached. in terms of Post Reach, the YouthWyze Zambia page showed that the reach was 7,870,240 (Post Reach) and 535,201 Post Engagement. The last two statistics are general and have no specific segmented age group that were attended to.

The program utilized school-based contact sessions, youth sports events, and community based outreach services to engage adolescents and young people. The program improved on the reporting by meeting the gender disaggregation of the data. However, the annual targets were not met due to limited contact as government orders restricted public gatherings in efforts to fight a nationwide cholera outbreak. The outbreak, which began in January 2023, continued into 2024 and became one of the most severe health crises in the country's recent history.

The targeted participants are 21000 females aged 10-24. Activities entail conducting of community dialogues to address cultural and religious barriers. Mobilize youth organizations to lead advocacy and awareness campaigns within their communities.

Number of CSOs included in Break Free! programme (2nd tier)
# of CSOs (not youth or women led) included in SPs programmes

description.narrative: This indicator serves to establish the reach of the programme by counting the number of civil society organisations (CSOs) that are not youth or women led and are 2nd tier partners in the programme, i.e., CSO partners directly contracted by any of the 1st tier partners within the scope of the implementation of the Break Free! programme.

comment.narrative: BF! is working with Chisomo, Young healthy, happy, and safe (YHHPS), and Restless development in Eastern province covering Kasangwa, Chipata and Chipangali districts. Restless development also has a presence at national level. The implementing partners have enabled the consortium to increase the reach of lobby advocacy against teenage pregnancy and child marriage and increased sexual and reproductive health services for adolescents and young people. The program is on track to achieve its five-year target for second tier organizations in the BF! Programme.
Chisomo and Young Happy Health & Safe are two CSOs working with the BF! programme in Eastern province's Chipata, Kasenengwa and Chipangali districts.

Chisomo Community Programme (CCP) and Young Happy Healthy & Safe (YHHS) have been BF! 2nd tier partners since 2021 and are operating in three districts in Eastern Province. Chisomo operates in Chipata and Kasengwana, and YHHS has operations in Chipata and Chipangali districts. YHHS is neither female or youth led. It aims to create a safe and supportive environment for adolescents and young people, empowering them to lead healthy and productive lives. The two implementing partners enabled the consortium to increase the reach of lobby advocacy against teenage pregnancy and child marriage and increased sexual and reproductive health services for adolescents and young people. They were instrumental in achievements such as the government reported dissolution of early marriages (https://www.eas.gov.zm/?p=10746).

These CSOs are targeted for inclusion in the collaborations with the BF! Programme to increase the reach of lobby and advocacy initiatives at the national level. The three CSOs are championing mental health programming and social accountability which have an important relation the BF! Programmme. The target is three based on the updated CSO mapping.

The Break Free has contracted two Community Based Civil Society Organizations. The organizations are based in Eastern province of Zambia. Of the two local CSOs, one (1)-Chisomo is a woman-led organization. The two CSOs are involved in Lobby and Advocacy activities.

title.narrative: Number of CSOs (not youth led) who report having strengthened lobby & advocacy capacities
# of CSOs (not youth or women led) with increased L&A capacities

description.narrative: This indicator tracks the number of CSOs that are not led by youth or women and record increased lobby and advocacy capacity. Break Free! programme has developed a standard capacity assessment tool to measure the change in targeted CSOs.

comment.narrative: The BF! programme will continue to improve the capacity of two implementing partners in Eastern province (Chisomo and Young Happy Health & Safe) increasing knowledge and awareness on advocacy and lobby

Disruptions from the cholera outbreak affected program activities. However, effort resulted in the achievement of the target and organizational gains in successfully developing capacities in resource mobilization, writing evidence-based program performance reports, mobilizing lobby and advocacy activists, networking, and public speaking among involved CSOs and CBOs.

The reported CSOs are BF! implementing partners who demonstrated increased knowledge and awareness on advocacy and lobby. Through their efforts, 18 young people have been co-opted in various strategic sub national and provincial Technical Working Group. additionally, 28 young entered a Social Contract making a commitment with traditional leaders and school authorities that they will not fall pregnant until they complete their education. The IPs also lobbied for establishment of Child Protection. Committees in two villages in the two schools that have high practice of child marriages.

Capacity strengthening of formal and informal youth and non-youth led CSOs partners will be guided by capacity assessments. Based on observations from 2021 and 2022 the programme is prepared to strengthen a variety of capacities, including, the use of evidence based advocacy through social accountability, awareness on national laws and policies, sexual and reproductive health and rights, leadership and governance, knowledge management, participatory M&E, budgeting and financial management.
The target of two non-youth led CSOs was achieved.
Chisomo and Young Happy Health & Safe are 2nd tier local CSO that are neither youth led or woman led.
